units: Roblox world studs, +Y up, +X east, -Z north (same as world/world.json and holes.json)
placement: For every instance: Model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(yaw), 0)); if scale is given use Model:ScaleTo(scale[2]) when the 3 values are equal, otherwise resize each MeshPart (Size and its offset from the pivot multiplied per axis). pos is the piece origin (base centre unless `origin` says otherwise). Every part FBX of a piece shares that origin.
import_settings: File > Import 3D, scale unit Stud, keep hierarchy; one MeshPart per material named <part>__<Material>; Anchored, CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch false (decoration only), CastShadow false on Neon/Water/Foam/Mist and on far pieces (mountains, far hills, clouds).
texture_note: Same textures/ as the props; world pieces use box UVs with tile_studs = prop tile x texture_tile_scale (listed per mesh).
fbx_export: same as props: Blender 4.5, unit NONE, axis_forward -Z, axis_up Y, FBX_SCALE_UNITS, embedded PNGs

pieces.notes: Giant hollow trunk shell around H9: outer r 45.84 (flared base), inner r 38.84, 100 tall, hollow up to y+78 under a dome with a 14-radius oculus shaft open through the top. Heartwood Door: 14 wide x 20 high arch at map angle 53.1 deg (splays to 17.5 wide inside). Parts 1-4 = trunk wall sectors (bark outside, warm Heartwood inside), 5 = buttress roots (to r 65.8, trimmed so they never touch H8/H9 felt, walls, walkways or lantern posts), 6 = outer details (door frame + lanterns, glowing windows, bracket fungi, moss), 7 = interior lantern strings / wall lanterns / glowing mushrooms (all far above or outside H9).
